sections.title: A diverse genus
sections.text: Veronica is a large, worldwide genus of annual or perennial herbs, ranging from low, creeping plants to upright forms; some Australasian members are shrubs. Leaves vary widely in shape and position, though opposite leaves are common in herbaceous species.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: Many species bear small four-lobed blue, purple, pink or white flowers in terminal or axillary clusters. Their fruit is usually a capsule. This plate is a plausible herbaceous speedwell, with opposite toothed leaves and blue four-lobed flowers, but it cannot represent the full genus; no general food or toxicity claim applies to every Veronica.
